A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and are readable throughout, with corresponding sections, equations, tables and figures identifiable. Neither contains an embedded appendix; supplementary grouping details mentioned in both are outside the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: Sections IV–V report original synthetic-image experiments, classifier accuracies, and bootstrapped causal-discovery results for bird classification and pneumonia detection.

after.justification: V3 retains the simulation and real-data experiments, revises bird causal-discovery results, and adds original LIME and SHAP demonstrations.

M1.justification: Both versions apply FCI to interpretable annotations and black-box predictions, imposing that predictions cannot cause the annotations. V3's numbered workflow restates this procedure; its additional assumptions and training disclosures do not establish a new algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: The synthetic shapes task, Caltech-UCSD Birds-200-2011 bird classification, and ChestX-ray8 pneumonia detection remain. The new LIME/SHAP examples use the existing image datasets and prediction tasks, without adding a distinct domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: V2 has no executed comparison against alternative explanation methods. V3 Section V.D evaluates LIME and SHAP, using Deep Explainer for SHAP, on both real-data classifier pipelines and presents their outputs in Figures 8–9.

E3.justification: Section V.B changes the bird FCI rejection threshold from 10^-5 to 0.05, materially revising graph selection. Section V.A corrects the reported bird training count from 2849 to 2489, consistent with the retained total of 3538. V3 also introduces qualitative image-level comparison procedures for LIME/SHAP. The split correction alone does not establish retraining.

E4.justification: Section V.D adds selected-image case studies examining whether LIME/SHAP highlights distinguish semantic characteristics such as wing shape versus wing pattern. These are limited qualitative analyses; no new ablation or robustness sweep is reported.

E5.justification: The bird conditional-independence tests use a changed rejection cutoff, from 10^-5 to 0.05. Otherwise, statistical reporting remains unchanged: 50 bird and 100 X-ray bootstrap replicates, the same edge-frequency stability measure, and no newly reported seeds or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Figure 5(a) replaces the bird stability values and rankings: Size, Eye Color and Bill Shape lead in v2, whereas Wing Shape, Wing Pattern and Tail Shape lead in v3. These results use different FCI thresholds. V3 also adds a bird PAG and LIME/SHAP outputs. The reported classifier accuracies and X-ray results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section III expands the informal internal-representation argument into an explicit structural causal approximation using partly unobserved high-level features and independent exogenous errors. It expressly imposes Markov, faithfulness and acyclicity conditions, substantially developing the assumptions supporting causal interpretation. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central claim remains that causal discovery can distinguish possible causes of predictions from confounded associations for explanation and auditing. The abstract is substantively unchanged. V3's explicit statement that it introduces no new algorithm matches v2's description of an approach based on existing tools; the new comparisons support the retained contribution.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands interpretation of the bird results, possible classifier tuning, domain-expert validation, and the limitations of local saliency explanations for co-located semantic features. Section VII newly emphasizes unknown causal ground truth and proposes realistic interventions and end-user studies as future validation.

D1.justification: Section V.A newly specifies cross-entropy loss, SGD, learning rate 0.001, momentum 0.9, and learning-rate decay by 0.1 every seven epochs. Section V.D supplies LIME/SHAP implementation links and identifies default settings and SHAP Deep Explainer. These disclosures do not establish changed optimization choices for the retained classifiers.

R1.justification: Six references are added, including SHAP, Guidotti et al., and counterfactual/recourse work by Lash, Joshi, Kanamori and Karimi. V3 expands discussion of LIME/SHAP relative to type-level causal explanation while retaining the broader causal-versus-associational positioning.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized language edits, clarifies type-level versus token-level terminology, adds a numbered workflow and Section V.D, and expands the introduction and conclusion. The main section sequence and much of the original prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds a bird PAG in Figure 6 and multi-image LIME/SHAP panels in Figures 8–9, substantially expanding the visual presentation. The original X-ray PAG remains as Figure 7. Figure 5(a) is reordered and rescaled; Table I and earlier illustrations are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: V3 makes causal assumptions and training settings explicit, corrects the bird split count, and adds visual comparisons and clearer validation limitations. These improve transparency and assessability. The comparisons remain illustrative, however, and the substantially different bird rankings under a changed threshold receive no sensitivity analysis or causal validation, limiting the overall evidential gain.
